steps: Unpack & check the packet

Unpack the fireplace, check the manual packet, unbolt the body from its wooden pallet and bend up the shipping clips. The glass latch tool, remote, backup battery holder, power harness and manual all stay with the homeowner.

Open the white manual-packet box; contact Mendota Technical Service if anything is missing.

Glass latch toolHA-77-00256
Remote transmitterHA-110-00105 · 3 AAA (65-06-01270)
Backup battery holder05-02-00345 · 4 AA (65-06-01147)
Backup power harness10-03-00128

These and the owner's manual must stay with the homeowner. Not included: log set, firebox inner liner and decorative front, each chosen and bought separately.

Net weight 325 lbs, so team lift. The four lifting handles (one each side, two on the rear wall) are for short moves only, never for carrying it. Inspect the unit on delivery and report freight damage within 48 hours.
LP conversion (if burning LP)

Fit kit HA-150-00011, ideally before the fireplace goes into its cavity: the motorized LP regulator, #59 left, #54 right and #56 pan burner orifices, and the pilot clip pushed in until "NAT" is hidden.

Qualified service agency only. Shut off the gas supply, then turn off the electrical supply. Work in a clean environment; correct operation isn't guaranteed if the kit or valve has been dropped or hit hard.
  1. Close the appliance service valve if the gas line is connected, and remove the 8 screws from the cover plate.
  2. With a Torx T20 (supplied) or slotted screwdriver, remove and discard the two regulator mounting screws, the regulator tower and the spring and diaphragm assembly (if fitted). Check the pre-fitted rubber gasket is in position.
  3. Fit the stepper-motor LP regulator with the supplied M4 x 0.7 screws, threaded by hand, then torque to 25 lb-in ± 5. Stripped valve threads: replace the valve. Put the identification label on the valve body where it's easily seen.
  4. Remove the left and right angled burners (4 screws each; marked "L" and "R") and the floor (2 rear screws). Fit #59 to the left burner, #54 to the right and #56 to the pan burner, each tightened securely.
  5. Pilot: hold its base with large vice grips, loosen the hood 1/4 turn counter-clockwise with a 7/16" open-end wrench (don't remove it), push the NG/LP clip fully in so "NAT" isn't visible, and retighten.
  6. Connect gas and confirm inlet and outlet pressures, fit the logs and glass door, and light with the remote: the main burner must light immediately without lifting, and pilot flames must be at least 1" long and overlap the propagation ports. Don't go on unless the burner cycles on/off without delays.

Attach the kit's labels to the back of the listing label plate in the air gap below the glass frame.

Note: the conversion steps put the pilot on the right side of the firebox (p. 52); the component guide puts it in the center of the firebox between the burners (p. 81).
Plan guides & hearth, set in the chase

Fit the finishing guides your front needs and plan the hearth pad, then set the fireplace in the framed chase on a wood, masonry or metal floor, level and plumb it, and secure it to the framing studs.

Finishing guides

  • The standard finishing guide suits any inside-finish decorative front; door kits use the guides supplied with the door kit. All guides stand 1" off the face; factory guides are riveted and come off with a ⅛" drill bit. Whichever guide is used stays permanently.
  • Grace, Mission and Willowbrook fronts: order the Flush Mount guide kit (front over the finish, screen recessed) or the Recessed Mount guide kit (front fits inside the guides; any finish material). Decide on the wall finish before the unit goes in.
  • Mask the glass frame and take off any front, screen or door before finish materials go on.
Note: p. 29 says wall finish deeper than 2 ½" requires the Recessed Mount guide kit, and also that the Flush Mount kit works with finish less than 3" thick, including backing, if reasonably flat.

Hearth pad and floor

  • The factory bottom guide sits 1 1/2" above the fireplace bottom. Build the hearth pad level with it, or raise the fireplace and cover the gap with non-combustible finish; a 4" pad means raising it 2 1/2".
  • Manufactured (mobile) home: bolt it to the floor and ground it.

Finish materials

  • Non-combustible zones need materials rated non-combustible per NFPA 220 or passing ASTM E 136. Paper-faced drywall (including Type X) and WonderBoard don't qualify, and WonderBoard off-gasses when heated.
  • Smooth walls: Promat Promafour or SkamoEnclosure Board, or Hardibacker 500 (two sheets for 1") with a Cool Wall system. Fix the boards to the wood framing and float them over the fireplace face, never screwed to it, with no seams above the fireplace.
  • Tile: unmodified dry-set mortar or hi-temp RTV silicone (48 hours cure minimum), not polymer-modified mortars; a non-combustible backer board is required in a non-combustible zone.
  • Stone: never a one-piece U-shaped surround. Facings outside the top air gap can reach 350 °F; heat-test marble, granite or polished stone samples at 275 °F to 350 °F for eight hours first.
Open the door; accent light
Release the two top spring latches with the glass latch tool and lift the glass door off. Next on the checklist: the accent light bulb and lens, which come installed in the unit.

1. Put the glass latch tool in the hole of each of the two top spring latches, pull toward you and turn 180 degrees to release. Leave the hooks upside-down for refitting.
  2. With both hands, tip the top of the frame out about 8", lift it 1" at an angle and set it aside. Check the glass gasket whenever the door comes off.

Accent light

The bulb holder is in a hole in the top metal baffle. Don't touch the bulb or lens with bare hands: use the bulb's foam wrap or clean cloth or neoprene gloves. Align the bulb base with the holder and push it all the way up, then fit the lens base gasket, lens, retainer bracket and four 10-24 nuts with a 3/8" hex hand driver. Don't over-tighten; that can crack the lens.

Bulb10-11-00020 · G9 Xenon, 25W
Lens10-11-00025
Lens retainer bracket with gasketHA-88-00168
Accent light housingHA-58-04606
Vent system & damper

Run UL Listed 5" × 8" coaxial rigid pipe of one brand and series within the master venting chart, every joint twist-locked and leak-proof with no silicone, then set the exhaust damper for the vertical rise.

Wall termination

  • Frame a 10-3/4" × 10-3/4" opening (a 9" hole is fine in a non-combustible wall). A wall thimble is mandatory through any combustible wall, and a combustible wall must be 4" to 8" thick maximum.
  • With the minimum 24" rise and a 90° elbow, the thimble center is 69 ½" above the fireplace floor level; add ¼" of rise for every foot of horizontal run. Never let the vent run downward.
  • Support horizontal pipe every 3 ft. The pipe ends flush with the outside wall; screw the cap to the wall and caulk it. Don't recess the cap into the wall or siding.
  • Use heat shield AA-11-00458 (or an equivalent) with vinyl, wood or other combustible siding.

Roof termination

  • Frame 10 ½" × 10 ½" ceiling openings with a fire stop spacer at every floor; cut a 10" × 10" roof opening; add an attic insulation shield; enclose the vent through occupied spaces above the first floor; wall straps every 3 feet.
  • Cap height above the roof: 2 ft from flat to 9/12 pitch, 4 ft at 10/12 to 12/12, 6 ft at 13/12 to 16/12, 8 ft at 17/12 to 21/12. Finish with the storm collar and vent cap.
Note: pp. 58 and 60 call for a 10 ½" × 10 ½" ceiling fire stop opening, but p. 60 also says the fire stop openings on upper floors are framed to 10" × 10" inside dimensions.

Cap clearances (from the cap center)

Above grade, veranda, porch, deck or balcony 12" (vinyl surfaces 24"); under a veranda, porch, deck or balcony 12". Openable window or door 12"; non-mechanical air inlet 12"; ventilated or unventilated soffit 18" (vinyl soffit 24"); outside corner 7"; inside corner 12" (vinyl 24"); service regulator vent 3 feet; mechanical air inlet 6 feet; public walkway or driveway 7 feet; never above a meter/regulator within 3 feet horizontally. Vertical caps: 24" horizontal clearance to any surface.

Two direct vent caps: 18" between centerlines; vertical caps close together need an 18-gauge or heavier galvanized barrier 6" taller and 3" wider than the caps. A wood-burning flue less than 36" away: a divider plate is recommended, or extend its liner 24" above the gas cap.

Vent damper

Seven notches, set with the glass latch tool at the rod above the glass frame (pull out about 1/8" and turn; clockwise closes). Notch 1 is fully open, notch 7 closed. With 10 ft of vertical rise close no further than notch 5; with 20 ft, notch 6; with 30 to 50 ft, any position.
Gas: connect, leak-test & verify
Bring a correctly sized line to the 1/2" NPT female inlet on the left side, set pressures at the valve taps, leak-test every field and factory joint, then verify orifice sizes and the input rate.

• Size the line from the supply regulator to the factory shut-off valve with the pipe-size table (see Gas supply pressure). Too small a line can cause improper burner ignition.
  • Recommended: a drip leg / sediment trap in the supply line. CSST flex line takes brass-to-brass fittings. Never plastic pipe.
  • Pressure-testing the supply piping: disconnect the appliance and its valve above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa); close its shut-off valve at 1/2 psi or less.
  • Leak-test all field-installed joints and the factory gas train joints with a gas sniffer or a soap and water solution.
  • Check pressures at the two taps on the main gas valve: supply 7" W.C. NG / 11" W.C. LP; manifold 3.5" WC NG / 10.0" WC LP (± 1/8").
  • Verify the orifice sizes stamped on the orifice bodies and clock the natural-gas input at the meter (see Input rates).
  • Where local code requires one, add an external keyed manual shut-off valve.
Power & backup DC inlet
Wire an always-hot 120 V supply (no switch in it) into the left-side junction box, then mount the backup DC power inlet box up to 5 feet to the left of the fireplace.

1. Remove the junction box cover plate (two screws) and route the house power cable through its strain relief.
  2. Strip the house wires and the color-coded wires in the box and join each color pair with the supplied wire nuts. Braided to braided: strip both ½" and twist. Braided to solid copper: strip the solid ½" and the braided ¾", and twist the braided around the solid.
  3. Use the plug labeled TO HOUSE POWER from the manual packet: house power plugs in at the back of the outlet box, into the plug toward the front of the fireplace. The plugs can't go in the wrong place. Tuck the wires in and refit the cover plate.
  4. Mount the DC inlet's single gang box within reach of its 6-foot harness, at most 18" to the box center or level with the room's other outlets. Don't staple the harness to the studs. Fit the white or beige cover plate, and the DC inlet decal once it's verified.

Ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Label all wires before disconnecting them for service. Show the homeowner how to connect the backup battery pack in an outage.
Liner, logs & air shutters
Install the firebox inner liner kit, then the Birch HD or White Oak HD log set, coals and inswool media per their own instructions, and set the three burner air shutters for the fuel.

Log sets: AA-11-05481 Birch HD or AA-11-05482 White Oak HD. Give the log set instructions to the homeowner. Logs and coals must not block the pilot or main burner flames.

Natural gasburner tubes 1/8" – 1/4" · pan burner 3/8" – 1/2"
Propaneburner tubes 3/8" – 1/2" · pan burner 3/8" – 1/2"

There are three tube air shutters, one for the floor (pan) burner and one for each angled burner, each adjusted on its own. Too blue: close in small 1/8" steps until a realistic yellow. Soot on logs or glass: open until it burns clean. Try each setting about ½ hr before changing again; very small changes make major differences. Above 4,500 ft some variation may be needed. Adjustments by a qualified installer, service agency or the gas supplier only.
Door on & test fire

Refit and latch the glass door centered in the opening, then test fire: the pilot must light immediately and light both front and rear burners, and the flame must be stable, not lifting, after 10 minutes.

• Glass gasket: the four gasket pieces must butt together at the corners, and the glass frame must latch properly.
  • Fresh batteries in the remote; synchronize it to the ignition module (master switch on, sync button, then On within seven seconds).
  • First burn: run the convection blower at level three for the first two hours, then let the fireplace cool before the curing cycle.
  • Burners light immediately and the flame runs promptly along the whole burner; the burner cycles on/off without delays.
  • Flame still lifting after 10 minutes: shut it off and check every vent pipe is twist-locked and leak-proof and the cap is right side up.
  • Damper: start at notch 1 (open) and burn at least 20 minutes. Short, fast-flickering flame: close it until the flame improves; closed too far, the flame lifts off the burner (ghosts) or soots. Burn at least another 10 minutes before further adjustments.
  • After a lockout, wait at least five minutes before relighting.
Cure & hand over
Run the 3-step curing cycle before finishing materials go on, train the owner on every function, leave the manual packet, complete the final checklist and register the warranty.

Curing

Barrier screen and any surround, front or doors on. Manual (OFF) mode, flame Hi, fan level 3 for at least 2 hours, then cool; flame Hi with the fan off until odors diminish (about 3 hours), leaving it on; then fan level 1 until any new odors fade. Expect smoke and strong odor: ventilate, and allow for smoke alarms. More than 10 continuous hours on high isn't unusual. Finishing materials in the non-combustible zone can see around 350° F.

Hand-over

Train the owner on the remote (IPI and CPI, flame, fan, accent light, rear burner, the three thermostat modes), lockout reset, the backup battery system, the master switch and the manual gas valve with the glass latch tool, removing the decorative front and glass door, the barrier screen requirement and periodic maintenance. Leave the manual packet, sign the final checklist with the homeowner and complete the warranty registration on mendotahearth.com.

panels.title: Soot on glass or logs
items: Burner air shutter closed too much → open it fully
Exhaust damper closed too far → open it
Improper log and/or ember placement
Glass door seal compromised: corners bulging, or the top-edge bulb white through its thickness
Incorrect gas pressure or orifice size: outlet 3.5" W.C. NG / 10" W.C. LP
Still sooting → shut it off and call a Mendota service person

panels.title: Pilot slow to light / keeps sparking
items: The pilot should light within five to eight seconds of sparking
Over ten seconds → check the pilot spark rod position and igniter wires for pinched or damaged areas
Sparking continues past five seconds after the pilot lights → dirty flame sensor; clean it with emery cloth
Still sparking → check the flame sensor lead wire for damage or grounding problems

panels.title: Delayed ignition, lifting or poor flame
items: Logs or coals blocking the pilot or main burner flame
Vent pipes not twist-locked and leak-proof, or the cap not right side up
Pilot flame not reaching the burners: 1" minimum, overlapping the propagation ports
Damper closed too far → flame lifts off the burner (ghosts) or soots
Short, fast-flickering flame → close the damper until it improves
Slow flame propagation → remove debris and vacuum the burner ports
Under-firing (orifices or pressure below nameplate) can cause delayed ignition

panels.title: Lockout
items: Pilot fails to light → system locks out; wait at least five minutes before relighting
Fireplace only beeps and ignores remote commands → may be in safety lockout
Frequent lockout → diagnose the primary cause; never assume the ignition control is faulty
Cold flue in winter → CPI raises startup draft and helps eliminate lockout

light.title: Turning it on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights its own pilot with an electronic igniter, using the remote. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before you start

  • Sniff all around the fireplace for gas, including down by the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low.
  • Make sure the master switch is on. It's at the bottom left corner of the fireplace, in the left-side air gap.
  • Keep the glass door on when you light it.

Light it

  1. Press On/Off on the remote. You'll hear a beep, then the igniter starts sparking.
  2. Once the pilot is lit and steady, the gas valve opens and the burners light at full flame.
  3. Turn the flame down to a level you like with the remote.

With the thermostat icon on OFF (manual), it lights and starts on Hi. On ON or SMART, it only lights if your set temperature is above the room temperature.

To turn it off, press On/Off again. No flame at all? It may be in lockout (see Won't light? Reset lockout).

Note: the manual says that with the master switch off only the main burners won't turn on and everything else, including the continuous pilot, still works (p. 69), and also that the remote won't communicate with the fireplace unless the switch is on (p. 74).

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote comes pre-programmed to your fireplace and takes 3 AAA batteries. Keep it within 20' of the fireplace. Every button press gives one beep; no beep means press again.

  • On/Off: lights or shuts off the fireplace.
  • Thermostat: OFF (manual, whatever the room temperature), ON (runs until the room is 1°F above your setting) or SMART (holds your setting by turning the flame up and down itself).
  • Mode: picks flame height, fan, accent light or rear burner.
  • Up/Down: changes that setting, or the set temperature.

Flame height and accent light have six levels; the fan has six speeds plus off. Down at flame level one turns the burners off. The rear burner setting switches only the left angled burner. For less heat, turn it off or lower the flame. On ON or SMART, the fan starts five minutes after the fireplace does and stops 12-1/2 minutes after the flames go out.

It shuts itself off after 24 hours on manual, or on ON or SMART after 60 minutes without hearing from the remote.

Child lock: press Mode and Up together; again to unlock. °F/°C: with it off, press Mode and Thermostat together. Re-pair: master switch on, press the sync button above it (three beeps), then On within seven seconds (four beeps).
Note: p. 71 says the remote's "AUX On" function isn't used on this fireplace; p. 72 says the Aux function switches an optional floor light or heat transfer kit.

curing.title: First fires: smoke and smell
curing.html:
The first fires burn off materials left from manufacturing and harden the paint, so smoke and a strong smell are normal. Your installer should run this curing cycle as the last step of the install, before finishing materials go on around the fireplace:

  1. Step 1: with the barrier screen and any front or doors fitted, set the thermostat to OFF (manual), flame on Hi, fan on level 3. Run at least 2 hours, then turn it off and let it cool.
  2. Step 2: same, but with the fan off. Run until the smell fades, about 3 hours, and leave it on.
  3. Step 3: set the fan to level 1. If new curing smells appear, keep running until they fade.
Open doors and windows. The smoke will set off smoke alarms. Running the fan in Step 1 keeps the smoke from staining the wall above.

More than 10 hours on high isn't unusual. Slight odors may return on later startups and fade with use.

Other smells

  • After three months or more unused: burnt dust and lint, like your furnace in the fall.
  • Adhesives, paints and wall finishes used wrongly around the fireplace can smell when heated.
  • An acrid smell can mean gaps in the glass gasket at the corners. Have it checked.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass now and then, and only once it has cooled to room temperature.

  • Outside: any glass cleaner you like.
  • Inside: take the glass door off first, then use Kel Kem Polish Plus (part # 65-06-00455) or a comparable product.
  • Never use oven cleaner or abrasive cleaners.
White film? The additives that make gas smell can harm the glass and leave a white film. It comes off if you clean it promptly.

Taking the door off

  1. Put the glass latch tool in the hole of each of the two top spring latches, pull toward you and turn 180 degrees to release. Leave the hooks upside-down; it makes refitting easier.
  2. With both hands, tip the top of the frame out about 8", lift it 1" at an angle and set it aside.
  3. To refit, set the two bottom tabs in their slots, center the frame, tip it in until the gasket touches, and re-hook both latches with the tool, hooks facing down.
Check the gasket every time the door comes off. Never run the fireplace with the glass off, cracked or broken, and don't strike the glass or slam the door. Glass replacement is for a licensed or qualified person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
An electronic igniter lights the pilot, and the pilot lights the main burners. You choose whether the pilot stays on between fires:

IPIpilot lights only when you call for heat, and stays on only while the burners run
CPIpilot stays lit; it shuts off after 7 days without use, and each use restarts the 7-day clock

To switch

With the remote off, press Mode. The screen shows CPI or IPI. Press Up for CPI or Down for IPI, then press On/Off to start the fireplace. A snowflake icon stays on the display in CPI.

In IPI, pressing Down at flame level one puts the pilot out too; in CPI the pilot stays on.

Why CPI in cold weather

A lit pilot keeps the chimney warm so it drafts well at ignition, stops excessive condensation on the glass, and keeps the fireplace body warm, cutting cold drafts and heat loss through the glass. It also helps prevent lockouts.

Note: the manual says CPI is required in winter when outside daily highs stay at 50°F or lower (p. 10), and recommends it when the average daily high falls below 50°F (p. 73).

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace normally runs on house power. In an outage, plug the backup battery pack that came with it (a holder with four AA batteries) into the backup power inlet: a wall plate to the left of the fireplace, marked with a decal.

On battery power the burner and flame height work, but the fan and accent light don't. The pack is 6V DC maximum. Keep the pack and its harness somewhere safe for the next outage; your installer should show you how they work.

With a Versiheat or FlexHeat heat transfer system (used to mount a TV above), the fireplace can't be run during a power outage.

Remote batteries

The remote takes 3 AAA batteries. Change them at least every 6 months, or more often with heavy use. A battery icon appears on its screen before they run out. Very weak batteries can make the fireplace shut itself off on ON or SMART.

Thermostat icon gone after a battery change? Take one battery out, hold the Thermostat button while you put it back, and look for "set" (enabled) or "clear" (disabled). Repeat until you see the one you want.

lockout.title: Won't light? Resetting lockout
lockout.html:
If the pilot doesn't light, the ignition system shuts down for safety. This is called lockout. If the fireplace only beeps and ignores the remote's commands, it may be in lockout too.

Quick reset

Press On/Off to turn the system off; that resets the lockout. Wait five minutes for any gas in the unit to clear, then press On/Off to try again.

Full reset

If the remote works but the fireplace still won't turn on:

  1. Turn the remote off.
  2. Turn it on and wait two seconds.
  3. Turn it off and wait two seconds.
  4. Turn it on and wait two seconds.
  5. Turn it off.

Then turn the remote on and start the fireplace. Check that the master switch is on.

In cold weather, CPI pilot mode keeps the flue warm and helps prevent lockouts. See Pilot modes.
Still won't run? Turn off the gas (see Gas smell & safety) and call your Mendota dealer, service technician or gas supplier. If lockout keeps happening, have your dealer find the cause; don't assume the ignition control is faulty.

safety.title: Gas smell, shutting down and hot surfaces
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone, and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Shutting it down

In an emergency, flip the master switch off to stop the main burners. To turn off the gas: press On/Off, turn off CPI pilot mode, close the manual gas valve in the left-side convection chamber (glass latch tool in the arrow-shaped bracket, turned down 90°), close any outside shut-off valve, and cut the power before any service.

Every day

  • The barrier screen must be on whenever the fireplace runs. Replace a damaged one with Mendota's barrier for it.
  • Keep furniture and other objects at least 60" in front of the barrier screen, and nothing on the front edge of the mantel.
  • The glass and nearby surfaces get too hot to touch. That's normal, but watch children and pets closely.
  • In a bedroom or other isolated room, always use a thermostat setting, never manual.
  • Never burn wood, paper or anything else in it, and keep flammables away.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Mendota requires replacing the whole appliance.

service.title: Yearly service and checks
service.html:
Have a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier service the fireplace at least once a year, in summer or early fall. Only they should adjust the burner, pilot or logs.

The yearly service

  • Clean lint and dust around the controls and blowers; check the wiring under the burner.
  • Clean the flame sensor and sparker rods; vacuum the pilot assembly and the burner ports. Insects drawn to the odorant in natural gas can nest in the burner ports and orifice areas.
  • Take out the logs and coals, clean the burner and logs, and check the logs for carbon.
  • Check the pilot and burner flames and the glass gasket.
  • Clear debris from the vent cap, and clean the glass and any enamel liner.

What you can watch for

  • Check the outside vent cap monthly for anything blocking it.
  • At full flame, after 30 minutes or more, the rear flame normally reaches 1 to 2 inches above the top of the rear log.
  • Carbon on the logs: turn it off and call a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier.
  • Soot patches bigger than 1" x 1" on the logs, a black film on the glass, or soot around the vent cap: turn it off right away and tell your Mendota dealer.

Lint from carpets and bedding can mean cleaning more often.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Mendota's limited lifetime warranty covers the original purchaser while the fireplace stays where it was first installed, and can't be transferred. It starts on the date Mendota invoices your installing dealer and only covers new units sold through an authorized Mendota dealer.

Which parts are covered, and for how long, is set out in a table on p. 87 of the PDF.

Making a claim

  • Report the problem to your Mendota dealer within 30 days, with proof of purchase, the purchase date, model name and serial number.
  • The serial number is on the listing label. Pull it out from the air gap below the glass door frame.
  • Your dealer submits the claim. If they can't help, write to Mendota at the address in the manual.

What can void or limit it

  • Installation or repairs by an unqualified person, or no permits and inspections.
  • Skipped annual maintenance, which is the owner's job.
  • Over-firing, neglect, water damage, or a serial number removed or made illegible.
  • After three years from dealer purchase, Mendota may settle by paying the initial owner the then-current wholesale price.

Parts you buy from your Mendota dealer after coverage ends carry a 90-day warranty with the receipt (no labor).

Discoloration, minor warping and noises as the steel expands and contracts are normal. Clean plated trim only with denatured alcohol, and wipe off fingerprints before the first fire.

specInput.title: Input rates and efficiency
specInput.html:
NG high / low fire44,500 / 24,000 BTUH
LP high / low fire44,500 / 26,000 BTUH
P.4 efficiency66%

Natural gas input check: verify the orifices and manifold pressure, turn off all other appliances and their pilots, and run 30 minutes at maximum flame, reading the meter before and after. (Final − initial, in therms) × 100,000 × 2 gives the input. The result must be at least the maximum input rate below 2000 feet (see the note), and at least 44,500 Btu above 2000 feet. For LP the manual checks orifice sizes and manifold pressure only.

Note: for altitudes below 2000 feet, p. 45 gives the maximum input rate as 45,500 Btu; the rating information (p. 15) gives 44,500 BTUH high fire, and p. 45 uses 44,500 Btu above 2000 feet.

Never over- or under-fire by changing orifice sizes or gas pressure; both void the warranty. Backyard natural-gas wells need gas analysis data sheets sent to Mendota before first firing. Above 7,500 ft, plan for input derating with the local gas company or Mendota Technical Service.

specInlet.title: Gas supply pressure and piping
specInlet.html:
Natural gas7" W.C. · 5.0" min / 11" max
Propane11" W.C. · 11" min / 13" max

Input and output pressure taps are on the main gas valve. Disconnect the appliance and its valve for supply-piping tests above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa); isolate it with its shut-off valve for tests at 1/2 psi or less.

Pipe size, supply regulator to the factory shut-off valve

Run (ft)Sch. 40 ID NG / LP · Type L OD NG / LP
0-101/2" / 3/8" · 1/2" / 3/8"
10-401/2" / 1/2" · 5/8" / 1/2"
40-1001/2" / 1/2" · 3/4" / 1/2"
100-1503/4" / 1/2" · 7/8" / 5/8"
150-2003/4" / 1/2" · 7/8" / 3/4"

The inlet is a 1/2" NPT female fitting, and the supply must enter the cabinet on the left side; supply a 1/2" NPT male fitting to connect. Never plastic pipe (some areas allow copper tubing or galvanized pipe). A drip leg is recommended; use brass-to-brass fittings on CSST flex line; leak-test with soap and water or a combustible gas sniffer. A manual shut-off valve is factory-installed in the left-side convection chamber; add an external keyed valve where local code requires one.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure, pilot and flame
specManifold.html:
Natural gas3.5" WC ± 1/8"
Propane10.0" WC ± 1/8"

Check at the output pressure tap on the main gas valve. The soot chart's pressure check uses the same outlet values (3.5" W.C. NG; 10" W.C. LP).

Pilot and burner checks

  • Pilot flames at least 1" long, overlapping the flame sensor and the burner propagation ports.
  • Pilot lights within five to eight seconds of sparking; it rectifies, and sparking stops, within five seconds.
  • Burners light immediately, without lifting, and flame travels quickly and smoothly along their full length.
  • At maximum, after 30 minutes or more, a normal rear flame is 1 to 2 inches above the rear log's top edge (depends on gas type, air shutter setting and venting).

specOrifice.title: Orifices and LP conversion kit
specOrifice.html:
NG · pan burner#47
NG · left / right angled burner#52 / #44
LP · pan burner#56
LP · left / right angled burner#59 / #54

Sizes are stamped on the orifice body. The fireplace ships for natural gas; LP kit HA-150-00011 holds one motorized LP pressure regulator (05-02-00346) and one each #54 (65-14-00054), #56 (65-14-00056) and #59 (65-14-00059) orifice. Mendota recommends converting the regulator, pilot orifice slider and burner orifices before the fireplace goes into its cavity. Qualified service agency only.

Note: p. 45 says natural gas uses #47 pan, #52 left and #44 right orifices at all elevations, including above 2000 ft, and LP uses #56, #59 and #54 at all elevations; the same page's high-altitude de-rating paragraph gives #38 (rear) and #44 (front) for natural gas and 1/16" (rear) and #55 (front) for propane at 2000-4500 ft.

Ask the local gas supplier whether high-altitude derating is needed; orifices may not need changing if the gas is already adjusted for altitude. When de-rating, fill in the High-Altitude De-Rating label from the manual packet and fix it, with any LP kit labels, to the back of the listing label plate in the air gap below the glass frame.

specFraming.title: Rough framing and enclosure
specFraming.html:
Enclosure width51"
Finished framing width45"
Height48 1/2"
Depth22-1/2"
Vent opening10-3/4" × 10-3/4"

Keep the 51" enclosure width so the fireplace sits centered; once it's in, the front of the enclosure can be framed to 45". Enclosure clearances: 1/2" at the sides and back, 0" from the top standoffs, and 55" from the unit bottom to the enclosure ceiling. Recessed in a cavity deeper than 22-1/2", all framing and finish protruding past the fireplace's front face must be non-combustible.

The ignition-system box protrudes from the left side; its front face is 3-5/8" in from the unit's front face. With the minimum 24" vertical pipe and a 90° elbow, the wall thimble center is 69 ½" above the fireplace floor level.

Set it on a wood, masonry or metal floor that runs its full width and depth, never directly on carpet, vinyl or other combustibles. On a cement slab, a layer of plywood may go underneath to stop cold conducting up. In a manufactured home, bolt it to the floor and ground it. Indoors only: protected from precipitation and excess moisture, with the ambient between 32°F and 110°F, or the warranty is void.

Net weight 325 lbs; team lift, and use the four lifting handles only for short moves. Build the chase like the home's outside walls: insulated, with vapor and air barriers, and fire stops and openings sealed with high-temperature caulk.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Direct vent to the outside only, on UL Listed 5" × 8" coaxial rigid pipe (5" exhaust, 8" air inlet) and approved caps, one brand and series throughout. A Mendota approved power vent is the other option.

Master venting chart

Vertical off the collar24" minimum
Rise 24" → horizontal max1'-6"
Rise 36" → horizontal max10'-9"
Rise 4 ft - 30 ft → horizontal max20'
Rise 31 ft - 50 ft → horizontal max50' - V
Vertical run50 feet max
Total straight pipe54 feet max
  • 90° elbows: up to 3 with a horizontal termination, 4 with a vertical one; take 3 feet off the allowed horizontal run for each 90° after the first.
  • Four 90° elbows: vertical cap only, at least 24 inches of vertical starter, and 9 feet off the chart's horizontal maximum when the starter is under 4 feet.
  • Two 45° elbows can replace one 90°; each horizontally positioned 45° takes 1½' off the horizontal maximum.
  • Clearance to combustibles: 3" above horizontal pipe and discharge elbows, 1" at the sides and bottom. Don't fill the air spaces with insulation.
  • Twist-lock every joint (about ¼ turn clockwise) leak-proof; no silicone at joints (stove gasket cement optional). Use fixed lengths over telescoping sections where possible.
  • No low-profile caps: they cause exhaust recirculation and ghosting flames. Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance; no common vents.
Note: p. 62 requires at least 24 inches of vertical starter for four 90° elbows (as does the master chart, p. 55), but its table is headed "V1(12" MIN.)" and starts with a 12" row.

Power vent: 4" × 6 5/8" pipe (reducer in the kit), 1' to 80' total, up to 6 90° elbows; kit AA-11-04071 for horizontal runs under 25 feet, AA-11-04072 over 25 feet, AA-11-04100 for vertical. 5" × 8" pipe needs the adapter with pressure tube 45-01-00424. Above 7,500 ft, contact Mendota technical service first.

specClear.title: Clearances, mantels and hearth
specClear.html:
Unit to floor0"
Unit to enclosure side / back wall1/2" / 1/2"
Unit bottom to enclosure ceiling55"
Unit bottom to room ceiling72"
Glass frame edge to adjacent side wall16"
Floor level to 8" mantel54"
Vent pipe top / sides / bottom3" / 1" / 1"

Side walls (p. 22)

Combustible side walls, corbels and mantel legs must sit behind a 45-degree line from the visible glass's side edges unless more than 16" away. NFPA 211 shielding cuts that 16" by 66% to 5-3/8" (20-gauge or heavier steel on 1" standoffs, open top and bottom, 12" larger each way than the heat source) or by 50% to 8" (R-1 ceramic or mineral board).

Note: the manual measures the 16" side-wall clearance from three different points: the side edge of the visible glass (p. 22 text), the glass frame edge (p. 15 clearance table) and the facing guide's side edges (p. 22 figure, "16" TO GUIDE EDGE").

Mantels (p. 23)

Measure from the fireplace floor level, or from the top of the convection air opening. Deeper than 8": use a 3:4 rise and run; the manual's example puts a 12" mantel 22" above the convection air opening (12" × 3/4 + 13"). Shallower mantels follow the approved mantel profile chart, which the manual shows only as a diagram.

Note: p. 23 gives the top of the convection air opening as 35 inches above the fireplace floor level, and a note on the same page gives the floor level to the top air gap as 34-7/8".

Hearth pad (pp. 24-25)

On the floor: non-combustible, R-1, at least 18" in front. Take 2" off its depth for every 1" the fireplace is raised; none is needed at 6" or more, though the floor in front can still reach 200 °F (raise it at least 12" over carpet, vinyl or laminate). No R-1 is needed under the fireplace. The factory bottom guide is 1 1/2" up, so a thicker pad means raising the fireplace.

Note: the R-value of mineral fiber board (Micore 160, 300, SB) at 1/2" is listed as 1.27 – 1.47 on p. 24 and 1.2 – 1.4 on p. 26. Rescor 360 (1.11) and Fiberfrax Duraboard LD (1.10) match on both pages.

TV above the fireplace (pp. 31-32)

Mantel at least 2" deeper and as wide as the TV, its top 12" or more above the top air gap (if the mantel is combustible, make certain the entire mantel meets the clearances to combustible mantels above); or a recessed cavity 6" taller and wider than the TV, its bottom 16" or more above the top air gap, TV set 2" in; or a Cool Wall, Versiheat (two fans) or FlexHeat system, which allow 12" with the convection fans turned off.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Supply120 VAC · minimum line voltage 110 VAC
Backup6V DC · battery holder 05-02-00345, 4 AA
Accent lightG9 Xenon, 25W · part 10-11-00020
Note: the manual gives two current ratings: 1.5 Amps in the rating information (p. 15) and 2 Amp in the AC power section (p. 38).

The supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it; ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. The junction box, with a strain relief clamp, is on the left side; join the house wires to the color-coded wires with the supplied wire nuts and use the TO HOUSE POWER plug from the manual packet. Label all wires before disconnecting them for service.

Backup DC inlet: the 6-foot harness lets the single gang box go up to 5 feet to the left of the fireplace, at most 18" to its center or level with the room's other outlets. Don't staple the harness to the studs. White and beige cover plates and a DC inlet decal are supplied.

Dual convection blowers are standard, rated 190 CFM in free air; on battery backup the fan and accent light don't run.

conflicts.issue: Master switch: p. 69 says that with it off only the main burners won't turn on and all other functions, including CPI, still operate; p. 74 says the remote won't communicate with the receiver unless the master switch is ON.
Aux function: p. 71 says the 'AUX On' function is not used in this fireplace; p. 72 describes the Auxiliary function turning an optional floor light or heat transfer kits on and off.

Winter CPI: p. 10 says it is required when outside daily highs remain 50°F or lower; p. 73 says Mendota recommends it when the average daily high falls below 50°F (the p. 86 checklist says 'suggested during cold season').

Natural gas input verification: the clocked result must be at least the 'maximum input rate (45,500 Btu)' below 2000 ft (p. 45), but the rated NG high fire is 44,500 BTUH (p. 15) and p. 45 itself uses 44,500 Btu above 2000 ft.

High-altitude orifices: p. 45 says NG #47 pan / #52 left / #44 right for 0-2000 ft and for all elevations exceeding 2000 ft, and LP #56 / #59 / #54 for all elevations; the high-altitude de-rating paragraph on the same page gives NG #38 (Rear) / #44 (Front) and propane 1/16" (Rear) / #55 (Front) for 2000-4500 ft (a two-burner rear/front layout, not this unit's pan/left/right).
Current draw: 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps in the ratings information (p. 15) vs 120 VAC, 2 Amp in AC Power Requirements (p. 38).

Top of the convection air opening: '35 inches up from the floor level of this fireplace' vs 'The distance from the Floor Level of this Fireplace to the Top Air Gap is 34-7/8"', both on p. 23 (affects mantel measurements; the 8" mantel at 54" on p. 15 matches 19" + 35").

Side wall clearance reference point: 16" 'from the side edge of the visible glass to a combustible side wall' (p. 22 text) vs 'GLASS FRAME EDGE TO ADJACENT SIDEWALL 16in.' (p. 15 table) vs '16" TO GUIDE EDGE' and 'at least 16 inches from the side edges of the facing guide' (p. 22 figure notes).
Mineral Fiber Board (Micore 160, 300, SB), 1/2": R-value 1.27 – 1.47 in the hearth pad board table (p. 24) vs 1.2 – 1.4 in the finishing materials table (p. 26).

Four 90° elbows: Prerequisite #2 requires a minimum 24 inches of vertical starter (p. 62; also note 1 of the master chart, p. 55), but the p. 62 table is headed 'V1(12" MIN.)' and its first row is V1 = 12" (H1+H2+H3 3', V2 max 50').

Ceiling fire stop opening: 10 ½" x 10 ½" (p. 58 step 3; p. 60 step 2) vs 'For multi-story vertical installation ... The opening should be framed to 10" x 10" inside dimensions as described in step No. 4' (p. 60; step 4 is the 10" x 10" roof opening).

Pilot location: 'Locate Pilot Light on the right side of the firebox' in the LP conversion steps (p. 52) vs 'The pilot is in the center of the firebox between the burners' in How to Access Components (p. 81).

Guide kit threshold: 'When the wall finish material will exceed 2 ½" in depth, the Recessed Mount guide kit will be required' vs the Flush Mount guide kit option 'requires that your finish material be less than 3" thick including backing materials and reasonably flat' (both p. 29).

review.notes: Catalog BTU (NG 44,500/24,000, LP 44,500/26,000), 66% P.4 efficiency, 5 x 8 vent, 325 lb weight, dual 190 CFM blowers, IPI ignition, ANSI Z21.88/CSA 2.33 and manufactured-home approval all match the manual (pp. 1, 6, 15, 19). Catalog height/width/depth (48.5 / 45 / 22.5) equal the manual's MINIMUM COMBUSTIBLE ROUGH FRAMING DIMENSIONS (height 48 1/2", finished framing width 45", depth 22 1/2"; pp. 15, 20), not necessarily the unit's own size; the dimension drawings (pp. 17-18) carry no text, so they can't be checked. Catalog viewing area (38" x 33 5/16") and 'hand-painted' log sets are not in the manual text. Shown only as figures/tables, not transcribed: appliance location / corner framing (Figure 3-1, p. 12), overall dimensions (pp. 17-18, no text), side wall figure labels (p. 22: '19-1/2" MIN. DEPTH', '47" MIN.', '11" HEAR...', '9" TO VENT PIPE CENTER'), the approved mantel profile chart (p. 23, referenced in specClear), approved vent system diagrams (p. 35, which also carries a 'MINIMUM 12" VERTICAL' label), the per-configuration vent tables (pp. 58-62; the p. 59 and p. 61 tables aren't tied to a configuration in the text, and p. 61's V1 rows read '2 ft.', '4 ft.', '4 ft. - 30 ft.'), power vent configurations and power vent exterior clearances (pp. 64-65, no text), PF2 ignition wiring diagram (p. 41), remote icons (p. 71), burner flame heights image (p. 80), parts diagrams (pp. 82-84), listing and warning labels (pp. 13-14) and the warranty coverage table (p. 87; the warranty drawer points to it instead of giving periods). P. 91 is blank. No LED/blink code table in the manual (only beeps), so codes is []. Fault panels come from the soot troubleshooting chart (p. 77), periodic inspection checks (p. 79), burner ignition characteristics (p. 53), the lighting checklist (p. 66), damper guidance (p. 63), over/under-firing (p. 80) and lockout guidance (pp. 10, 71, 74, 80). Minor discrepancies not flagged in drawers: fan run-on is 12-1/2 minutes on p. 70 but 12 minutes in the p. 86 checklist (guide uses 12-1/2); burners are called 'rear and front' (pp. 53, 66, 76, 79) although the unit has pan, left and right burners, and the remote's 'rear burner' control shuts off only the left angled burner (p. 72; the remote drawer says so); p. 66 says 'Four distinctive wood species log sets' but lists two (Birch HD, White Oak HD); the installation checklist (p. 46) says to install the accent light bulb and lens while p. 49 says they come installed (step 3 reflects both); the listing label hangs on a chain (pp. 13-14) or a cable (p. 75); the FAQ (p. 76) calls house power 110VAC while the electrical sections say 120 VAC (owner drawer just says 'house power'); p. 74 says the door must remain on during pilot ignition 'except for the First Time Lighting' (the owner drawer just says keep the door on, given the pp. 6-7 warnings against operating with the glass removed); CPI is called Continuous Pilot Mode (pp. 10, 69) and Pilot on Demand (p. 73), so the guide uses 'CPI'; the lockout reset is given two ways (p. 74: On/Off, then wait five minutes; p. 78: off/on sequence), both shown; p. 50 calls the unit a 'Fireplace Insert'; p. 12 gives the R-1 hearth pad as '1-1/2" Thick Maximum' while p. 25 allows a thicker pad if the fireplace is raised (guide follows p. 25's bottom-guide explanation); the °C/°F steps on p. 78 are numbered 4-6 and say 'repeat Step 2'. The lighting checklist (p. 66) says to follow the 'First-Time Lighting Instructions' to synchronize the remote, but the sync steps are under Synchronizing the Fireplace and Remote Control (p. 69); the guide uses p. 69's steps. Finish-material guidance in step 2 comes from pp. 26-28; TV recommendations in specClear from pp. 31-32. Website check (Oct 12): every website.json figure the manual covers (BTU ranges, P.4 efficiency, the four framing figures) matches the guide; the viewing area isn't in the manual text, so no website notes were added.
